top_five: Split the one long page into real pages (home, /tropos, /lighting, /mantle, /colors/{name}, /studio, /inquire), with the color in the URL. Make /tropos the flagship: coins that recolor every picture, an eight-view gallery, the 360, sound, the uplit base, specs in inches, 'Goes with', and an inquiry pre-filled with the chosen color.

Render one consistent set of pictures with the new Tropos, the redesigned Mantle and the cordless Core: the hero lineup in desktop and phone frames, studio shots of each product in all eight colors on one seamless, close-ups, the uplit eight and the room. Take every superseded design off the site.

Rebuild the hero as one full-height frame: 'A world of sound, in color.' set on the picture, the speakers filling about 55% of the window and named at their feet, a single 'Explore Tropos' button, a separate phone render where the speakers are legible, and a line about the speaker instead of a description of the picture.

Replace the three-screen pinned light section with one coin-driven stage followed by the uplit eight. Cut the colors from six appearances in three swatch styles to one coin component used in two places on the home.

Give visitors something to do and someone to trust: an inquiry form, a 'Hear first' sign-up, a Studio page with the people and one real photograph of the acrylic, a sample set of the acrylic coins, and the render note as a single footnote.
critic:ux.direction: I'd build a small, fast site of several pages: a home page that plays like a launch film, and product pages that work like a design store. The home has six beats: the named lineup under 'A world of sound, in color.'; the uplit eight at night; three product tiles; one color chapter, where a coin fills the screen with that color's habitat and tagline and recolors the trio; the room, for scale; and 'Hear first'. Tropos gets the flagship page: coins that recolor every picture, a gallery, the 360, 'The oldest amplifier is a shape.', the uplit base, specs with a to-scale drawing, 'Goes with', and an inquiry pre-filled with the chosen color. Each color gets its own page, and Studio carries the people, the progress and the real material. From Apple's 24-inch iMac page (apple.com/imac), take how to sell one object in many colors: the lineup hero, a color picker that swaps the product in place, full-bleed color moments, one idea per section, disclosures as footnotes, and specs on a page of their own. From Teenage Engineering (teenage.engineering, the OP–1 field and OB–4 pages), take the voice (dry, exact, quietly funny), plain studio photography on one ground, and spec pages that make hardware feel serious and lovable. From Farrow & Ball's color pages (farrow-ball.com), take the idea that every color is a named, numbered page with a short story, suggested pairings and a sample you can order. That maps onto EARF's eight colors, the founder's same-color and opposite-color pairings, and the acrylic coin as the sample.

issues.where: desk-01.jpg, desk-02.jpg, desk-04.jpg, desk-06.jpg, desk-07.jpg, desk-09.jpg; phone-01.jpg, phone-02.jpg, phone-07.jpg, phone-08.jpg
issues.problem: There are seven unrelated picture worlds on one page: a paper-studio lineup (hero), a pink-dusk grass field (Tropos card), a peach gradient void (Hemisphere card), a white e-commerce packshot (Mantle card), uplit concrete at night (light section), CG lava and desert (habitats) and a sunlit living room. Camera height, lens, light direction, color temperature and grade change from frame to frame. Each product line is shot in a different visual language, so the range never reads as one family cut from one material. Several frames read as renders rather than photographs: the lava in desk-07, the smeared, blobby mesa in the Dust card beside it, and the Mantle floating on white in desk-02. Vitra's or B&O's pages look like the work of one photographer; this looks like seven separate briefs.
issues.fix: Write a one-page shot bible and re-render every home-page picture to it with the new speaker. Nothing goes live that breaks it. STUDIO, for every product and line picture: a seamless in the page's own paper (#F4F1EC) so the frame edge disappears; one large soft key high left plus a weak fill, from the same direction in every frame; camera at product mid-height; about an 85 mm lens; the product filling 70% of the frame height. NIGHT, for everything after dark: exactly the uplit board-formed concrete set in desk-06 and phone-07. WORLD, for the habitats: one film grade (filmic tone curve, fine grain, real lens depth of field, atmospheric haze, a little halation). Run all three through one color pipeline so Ember is the same red everywhere. For how to light tinted transparent material (the color living in the light it throws, caustics on the ground), study Sabine Marcelis's photographs of her resin work. Retire the grass field, the gradient void and the white packshot.

issues.where: desk-01.jpg, desk-02.jpg, desk-03.jpg, desk-09.jpg, desk-10.jpg; phone-01.jpg to phone-03.jpg, phone-09.jpg, phone-10.jpg; live-text.txt
issues.problem: The copy still does what the founder ruled out: it states the obvious ('Tropos is a horn loudspeaker cast in tinted acrylic, in eight colours from Ember to Smoke', 'A powered horn loudspeaker in eight colours of cast acrylic', 'A record player in the same eight colours', 'Eight colours, every line', 'Covers on, by a tall window'). One wanders.'; the light chapter, 'Leave a light on.' over 'A light in the base fills the cabinet to its edges.' (the new uplit base makes 'Put a light under it' wrong); each habitat captioned with its color's line ('Ember. The last light of the fire.', 'Poison. Bottle green, with a hint of menace.'); at home, 'A pair in Poison.' with the size as the only caption; contact, 'Write to us.' over 'Each pair is made to order. issues.where: desk-01.jpg, desk-02.jpg, desk-03.jpg, desk-07.jpg, desk-09.jpg, desk-10.jpg; phone-01.jpg, phone-02.jpg, phone-08.jpg, phone-10.jpg
issues.problem: The interface uses a tech-startup kit, not a design house's: black and outlined pill buttons ('See the speakers', 'Copy address', 'Menu'), letter-spaced monospace eyebrows over every headline, rounded cards with gray caption panels, a round carousel chevron sitting on a photograph, and the email address in monospace next to a copy button. 'PROGRESS' is set in a bolder proportional sans while every other eyebrow is monospace. Every headline is the same bold, tightly tracked grotesk at about the same size and position, so nothing is ever loud and nothing is ever quiet; the largest word on the page is 'Ember' in the dark band. Image corners are rounded in the cards and habitats but square in the room.
issues.fix: Strip the kit. Replace the pill buttons with text links in the body face, underlined at 1 px with a 4 px offset. Use no monospace on the home page (keep it, if anywhere, for the spec table). Show images square-cut or full-bleed only, put captions on the page ground with no gray panels, and remove the carousel chrome. Rebuild the type scale around real contrast: display at clamp(48px, 8vw, 128px), in Regular rather than Bold and tracked about −1%, used for only three moments (the hero, the light chapter and the contact). Set everything else at 18 px for text and 13 px for captions, in the same family. If a second voice is wanted, add one high-contrast serif for display only (something like GT Super or Editorial New), and never pair a serif with a mono.

issues.where: desk-07.jpg, desk-08.jpg; phone-07.jpg, phone-08.jpg
issues.problem: The most ownable idea on the site is each color shown in its own world. That is exactly what 'A world of sound, in color', the name EARF and the globe mark all promise, and it is buried in a carousel. One card and a sliver of the next are visible, and six of the eight sit behind a chevron few visitors will press. The peeking Dust card is washed out by a white gradient that looks like a rendering fault, over a mesa with blobby, smeared edges. The one visible frame (Ember on lava) looks like a game level, not a film still.
issues.fix: Make the habitats the spine of the page: eight full-bleed frames in sequence (100svh on desktop, 4:5 at full width on phone). Set each color's name and line small at lower left, and run a quiet index of the eight names along the edge to show where you are. top_five: Write one shot bible (STUDIO on the page's own paper, NIGHT on the uplit concrete, WORLD for the habitats, all in one grade) and re-render every home-page picture to it with the new speaker. Retire the grass field, gradient and white packshot in desk-02 so the range reads as one family.

Get rid of the empty screens. Make the light stage exactly one screen tall, never empty and ending on the uplit lineup (desk-05 and phone-05/06 are black), show the eight habitats as full-bleed chapters instead of a carousel, and show the palette once instead of three times.

Rewrite every line to say one thing, once, with a wink: no eyebrows, no 'eight colours'/'acrylic' refrain, the color taglines and 'The oldest amplifier is a shape.' back in view, a Sound chapter to back the new tagline, and American English throughout.

Swap the startup kit for a design house's (no pill buttons, mono, cards, chevrons or rounded corners; lighter display type with real contrast in scale). Close on a Studio chapter of real evidence (acrylic chips in window light, a drawing, the founder's name) and a form that records interest by product and color.
critic:creative-director.direction: I'd build a slower, quieter page led by pictures: one full-bleed image per screen and at most one line of words with it. The order: the new Tropos lineup on warm paper carrying 'A world of sound, in color.'; Sound (the horn in section or turning silently, 'The oldest amplifier is a shape.', three design figures); after dark (a one-screen uplit stage, color by color, ending on the eight lit against concrete); the world (the eight habitats full-bleed, each with its line); at home (the pair in a room, then Hemisphere and the cordless Core in one frame, then the new Mantle once it exists); Studio (real chips in window light, a fabrication drawing, the founder's name, a dated progress line); and Write to us, with a form. Keep the paper ground, the lineup in spectrum order, the uplit concrete set, the color names and the honest tone. Lose the pill buttons, the mono, the cards, the carousels and the eyebrows. From Apple's iMac page (apple.com/imac, the 2021 color launch), take the mechanic: color is the interface, choosing one swaps the full-frame picture in place, and each screen holds one idea at heroic scale. From Aesop (aesop.com), take the voice and the restraint: dry, literate lines said once, captions doing the work, text links instead of buttons, no ornament. From Bang & Olufsen (bang-olufsen.com, the Beolab 90 and Beolab 50 pages), take the scale and the sound story: the product at architectural size in every frame, material in close-up, and sound told one figure at a time.

Back up 'A world of sound, in color.' with a Sound band after the hero (why a horn, the cutaway, four design-target figures, inputs). Launch it in one release with the new tagline, American English and the new speaker set, all on one art direction, so no superseded design stays on the page.
critic:credibility.direction: Today it reads as a capable designer's render portfolio rather than a company: strong pictures, but no people, no dates, no way to sign up and nothing about sound. I would build a shorter, more confident site in three layers. The home page runs about six screens: the new lineup under 'A world of sound, in color.' with one action, Hear first; a Sound band (why a horn, the cutaway, four design-target figures); one color moment where choosing a coin lights the speaker and opens a color page with every line in that tint; the room, re-rendered with three lines in one color; a dated Progress strip with real artifacts; Studio; and the sign-up. The uplit row and the room stay, since they are the strongest pictures. Next comes a page per line: a hero on the shared seamless, a color selector, six consistent views, materials and making, a specs table in inches and millimeters, and 'Made to order. Price on request.' Last, Studio, Journal and Press pages, so the company can be checked and covered, with the habitats living in the journal as a campaign. From Analogue (analogue.co), take the product discipline, especially how it presents its tinted transparent editions: one object on a flat ground, each color treated as a named product, specs as a clean table, and a calm notify-me state before anything is for sale. critic:copy.direction: I would build a shorter home page in three acts and leave the detail to the product pages. Open on the new eight, lit from behind, full screen, with “A world of sound, in color.” and one plain line. Act two is sound: one Tropos on the studio seamless, turning as you scroll, “The oldest amplifier is a shape.”, three figures and a way to its page. Act three is light and color: the uplit eight, then one row of acrylic coins that recolors everything below it (the speaker lit, its habitat and line, and Hemisphere, Core and Mantle in the same color), replacing today's five rows. Then the room, Progress with one real photograph, and a sign-up to close. From Apple's iMac page (apple.com/imac), take the system for one object in many colors: a picker that changes the product where it stands, a short headline followed by one plain sentence, and scroll-driven motion that is a finished picture wherever it stops. From Teenage Engineering (teenage.engineering), take the house discipline and the deadpan: every object on the same ground in the same light, products listed by name, specs stated flatly, and copy that is funny because it never tries to be. From Aesop (aesop.com), take the restraint: few words, no instructions, wide margins, and a page that trusts the reader to get the joke.

top_five: Show the product big and close. Make the hero one screen with the cast at 40% or more of its height, plus its own phone render (today the cast is about 120 px tall on a phone). Put the owner's turning view right after it, and build object pages with close-ups, particulars and 'Price on request'. The live page ends at 'Write to us.' without any of them.

Sell the sound: a cutaway of the horn, three design-target figures and one line on why a horn ('The oldest amplifier is a shape.'). Today there isn't a word about sound on a speaker brand's page, and 'A world of sound, in color.' can't stand on that.

Make color one system instead of three dot rows: rendered acrylic chips from one token set, the hero legend gone, 'By colour' turned into a family viewer with all four objects in the chosen color, and the light band cut from 3.7 screens to under 2 with no black runway.

Rewrite the copy to rules: 'eight colors' once, no caption that restates the picture, every line adds sound, scale, making or how to order, American English throughout, and the render disclaimer moved into quiet per-image credits.

Give the launch a list and a face: a 'Join the first run' form (email plus color) in the hero, header and footer; Progress with the exploded drawing, dates and the first real photograph; a founder and studio line; and a full footer.
critic:skeptic.direction: Two layers instead of one long scroll: a home page of about seven screens that tells one story, and a page for each object that carries the depth. Home, in order: the cast, at full presence, under 'A world of sound, in color.' with one button, 'Join the first run'; one Tropos turning, with chips beneath; the eight lit, full-bleed; Sound (a cutaway, three figures, 'The oldest amplifier is a shape.'); color families, where a chip swaps one studio frame of Tropos, Hemisphere, Core and Mantle in that color; one room, cropped tight; Made (the exploded drawing, dated steps, the first real photograph) and the sign-up again. Object pages: sticky chips, gallery, close-ups, turning view, particulars, 'Price on request'. From Apple's AirPods Max and iPhone pages, take the color picker that recolors the product in place, one idea per screen, and specs kept on their own page so the story stays short. From Teenage Engineering's OP–1 field pages, take objects shot full size on a plain ground, particulars set as a design element (the one honest use for the monospace), and wit kept to a word or two. From Devialet's Phantom pages, take how to make sound visible: an exploded view and the physics reduced to one big image and a few numbers.
